constraints.decision: How the tool is installed: The tool is written in Python 3 and installed with pipx from the repository: pipx install "git+https://github.com/lovaizu/playground.git#subdirectory=downloads-organizer", needing Python 3.9 or later and pipx, which a reader may first install with brew install pipx or sudo apt install pipx.

Licence: The tool is under the MIT licence, in a LICENSE file at downloads-organizer/LICENSE, which the README's licence section points to; the rest of the repository is not touched by it. Who the copyright line names is still to be settled when the LICENSE file is made.

constraints.chosen: The README's Development section links to downloads-organizer/docs/development.md, a development document made at the architecture or the build stage for whoever builds or changes the tool (code layout, running the tests, the way to the architecture): the user decided it, kept as the plan's decision 'Development document', when turn's generator asked

The README links to downloads-organizer/LICENSE and downloads-organizer/docs/development.md as they are, with no words saying they are not there yet; the build stage makes both files before the README is merged and checks that every link of the README leads to a file: the decisions 'Licence' and 'Development document' already say both files are made later and linked to, and words saying 'not yet there' would go stale

constraints.decision: What --help shows: downloads-organizer --help prints each way to run the tool and the extensions each group holds, so the extensions are listed in the tool alone and the README points to --help for them.
